why: task lists everywhere, options, entry point, docs, tests and changelog
prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The `tasklist` extension is added and registered, so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works; the full suite passes (1154 tests, 112 skipped), including 25 new tests. flake8 and the docs spelling/link checks are not installed here, so they were not run. Things you might not expect: (1) a bare `- [x]` with no text after it is left as plain text, because the marker must be followed by a space; (2) in the default xhtml output the checkbox renders as `<input checked="checked" disabled="disabled" type="checkbox" />`, and as `<input checked disabled type="checkbox">` with `output_format='html'`; (3) an empty `item_class` adds no class; (4) `docs/extensions/index.md` still carries the existing note that no new extensions will be added to the project, which this extension now contradicts — I left that note untouched; (5) the changelog entry is under a new `[Unreleased]` heading and has no issue number, since there is no issue to reference.
